test.title: Solutions - Test 5
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text:
The number of units, which are used to express concentration of solutions from the following is _________.

(Mass percent, Mole, Mole fraction, Molarity, ppm, Molality.)

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>224</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>SO</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></msub></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>298</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>atm</mi></math> is passed through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><mi>NaOH</mi></math> solution. The non-volatile solute produced is dissolved in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of water. The lowering of vapour pressure of solution (assuming the solution is dilute) (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><msub><mo>°</mo><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mfenced></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hg</mi></math>) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hg</mi></math> the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is <u>              </u> (Integer answer)

At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, the vapour pressure of benzene is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>70</mn></math> torr and that of methyl benzene is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> torr. The mole fraction of benzene in the vapour phase at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> above an equimolar mixture of benzene and methyl benzene is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> (Nearest integer)

An artificial cell is made by encapsulating \(0.2 \mathrm{M}\) glucose solution within a semipermeable membrane. The osmotic pressure developed when the artificial cell is placed within a \(0.05 \mathrm{M}\) solution of \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) at \(300 \mathrm{~K}\) is _______ \(\times 10^{-1}\) bar. (nearest integer).
[Given : \(\mathrm{R}=0.083 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{bar} \mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}\)]
Assume complete dissociation of \(\mathrm{NaCl}\)

Molality of 0.8M H2SO4 solution (density 1.06 g cm-3 ) is _______×10-3 m.

Round off your answer to the nearest integer.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute is disolved in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of two different solvents <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> whose ebullioscopic constants are in the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>8</mn></math>. The elevation in boiling points of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> are in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></mfrac><mfenced><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>:</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></math> is____(Nearest Integer)

If the concentration of glucose C6H12O6 in blood is 0.72 gL-1, the molarity of glucose in blood is -×10-3M (Nearest integer):
[Given : Atomic mass of C=12,H=1, O=16 u]

A cylinder containing an ideal gas ( 0.1mol of 1.0dm3 ) is in thermal equilibrium with a large volume of 0.5 molal aqueous solution of ethylene glycol at its freezing point. If the stoppers S1 and S2 (as shown in the figure) are suddenly withdrawn, the volume of the gas in litres after equilibrium is achieved will be _____________.
(Given, Kfwater=2.0Kkgmol-1,R=0.08dm3atmK-1mol-1

A solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>31</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>%</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> by mass and has a density of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>mL</mi></math>. The molarity of the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> solution is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> (nearest integer) [Given molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>98</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

Lead storage battery contains 38% by weight solution of H2SO4. The van't Hoff factor is 2.67 at this concentration. The temperature in Kelvin at which the solution in the battery will freeze is _____ (Nearest integer).

Given Kf=1.8 K kg mol-1

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>004</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> solution is isotonic with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> glucose solution. Percentage dissociation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> is _____ (Nearest integer)

A solute A dimerizes in water. The boiling point of a 2 molal solution of A is 100.52C∘. The percentage association of A is ___ .
(Round off to the Nearest integer)

 Use : Kb for water =0.52 K kg mol-1 

            Boiling point of water =100°C

If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>250</mn><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>of an aqueous solution containing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>73</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of a protein <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is isotonic with one litre of another aqueous solution containing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>65</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of a protein <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>,</mo></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>298</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>, the ratio of the molecular masses of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>_</mo><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> (to the nearest integer).

Elevation in boiling point for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> molal solution of glucose in water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. The depression in freezing point for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> molal solution of glucose in water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. The ratio of molal elevation constant to molal depression constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> is

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>150</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of acetic acid was contaminated with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> ascorbic acid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> to lower down its freezing point by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is____ (Nearest integer). [Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>; Molar mass of ascorbic acid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>176</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

Mass of Urea NH2CONH2 required to be dissolved in 1000 g of water in order to reduce the vapour pressure of water by 25% is _______ g. (Nearest integer)

Given : Molar mass of N, C, O and H are 14, 12, 16 and 1 g mol-1 respectively.

In a solvent <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of an acid HA dimerizes and the rest dissociates. The van't Hoff factor of the acid is _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> (Round off to the nearest integer)

If the degree of dissociation of aqueous solution of weak monobasic acid is determined to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, then the observed freezing point will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math> higher than the expected/theoretical freezing point. (Nearest integer).

The osmotic pressure of a solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>NaCl</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>10</mn></math> atm and that of a glucose solution is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>20</mn></math> atm. The osmotic pressure of a solution formed by mixing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> of the sodium chloride solution with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> of the glucose solution is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> atm. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is ________ (nearest integer)

A solution containing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> of a solute dissolved in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>75</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> of water boils at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>373</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>535</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. The molar mass of the solute is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>·</mo></math> [nearest integer] (Given : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></msub><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>52</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and boiling point of water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>373</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>)
